findings.what: Runbook gives no 'node -v' / 'nvm use' step. The default shell of the machine that produced the evidence is Node v18.20.7 (FINAL report itself says 'Node 18 par défaut dans le shell'). 'npm start', 'npm run seed:demo' have NO check-node preflight (only pretest/pretypecheck/prebuild/pretest:e2e have it), so on Node 18 the presenter gets a cryptic 'node: bad option: --env-file-if-exists=.env' instead of the friendly message. The report's sentence 'refusé par les contrôles préalables' is true only for test/build, not for the commands the presenter actually runs.
findings.evidence: node -v -> v18.20.7 in this environment; node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --env-file-if-exists=.env -e 0 -> 'node: bad option: --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning'; be/package.json scripts: start/seed:demo/dev have no pre* hook; only root has .nvmrc.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'nvm use (reads .nvmrc); node -v must print v22.18 or higher' to script 2.1 and README; optionally add prestart/preseed:demo hooks running scripts/check-node.mjs; qualify the FINAL report sentence.

Clinical-logic gap not stated in the backlog: bio-01 presents an oliguric post-operative patient with creatinine 4.2 and then asks (S3) 'Before calling it, which action best rules out pseudohyperkalemia?'. In true AKI, K 6.1 is probably real; teaching 'confirm on a non-hemolyzed sample' as THE action without the clinical-context step (ECG, immediate clinical communication, treatment not delayed) can model delay of a critical-value communication. The backlog C-01 covers the notify/confirm order but not the pre-test probability argument (hemolysis is not evidenced anywhere in bio-01, see C-02). Marked PLAUSIBLE: depends on local critical-value SOP.
findings.evidence: c:196 'reduced urine output after surgery', c:199 creatinine 4.2/BUN 62, c:209 K 6.1 HH, c:217-222; no hemolysis index in bio-01 data.
findings.suggested_fix: Ask the biochemist in question 1 of section 6 to rule on: communicate immediately AND confirm; add an explicit hemolysis index or an ECG/clinical-context clue to bio-01.
